key_insight: A high-order multiscale method captures wave propagation in heterogeneous composites with fractional damping while achieving a global O(ε) energy-norm error bound.
engineering_relevance: The method reduces the computational burden of simulating composite structures with fine-scale material variations and history-dependent attenuation.
method: Derive a homogenized wave equation with first- and second-order multiscale corrections.
Combine finite elements and finite differences using a fully discrete L2-1σ–Newmark scheme.
Establish local residual cancellation, global error bounds, and unconditional shifted-energy stability.
evidence_signal: Two- and three-dimensional numerical examples demonstrate accuracy, efficiency, reduced computational cost, and robustness, though the abstract reports no quantitative speedups.
watch_item: Practical implementation must still address the storage and computational demands of fractional-history terms.
paper_title: A high-order multi-scale method and its error analysis for nonlocal-in-time fractionally damped wave problems in composite materials
